title: Understanding Bulk Modulus
text: The bulk modulus $$B$$ is a measure of a substance's resistance to uniform compression. It is defined as the ratio of the change in pressure ($$\Delta$$P) to the relative change in volume ($$\Delta$$V/V).

title: Relating Bulk Modulus to Volume Change
text: The formula for bulk modulus is given by: B=-($$\Delta$$P)/($$\Delta$$V/V). Rearrange this formula to find the change in volume ($$\Delta$$V).

title: Finding the New Volume
text: The initial volume $$V$$ of the sphere can be calculated using the formula for the volume of a sphere: $$V=(4/3)\pi*r$$**3, $$where$$ $$r=0.2\, \text{m}$$.

title: Relating Volume Change to Radius Change
text: The change in volume ($$\Delta$$V) can be related to the change in radius ($$\Delta$$r) using the derivative of the volume formula: $$\Delta$$V=4*$$\pi*r$$**2*$$\Delta$$r.
